summary: Learn to quantify disaster risk, build response models, and report resilience with confidence. Enroll in practical 5-day training.
lede: Quantitative risk models for disaster and crisis management provide a structured way to estimate hazard likelihood, assess consequences, map exposure, and prioritize resilience actions. This course helps you turn field knowledge into defensible risk decisions through scenario analysis, quantified risk matrices, risk registers, and mitigation tracking. You will work through practical methods for impact and likelihood scoring, business impact analysis, critical-function mapping, recovery prioritization, and dashboard reporting. The course also introduces Monte Carlo simulation concepts and automated monitoring use cases at an operational level, helping you communicate credible recommendations when data, budgets, and resources are limited.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with crisis planning, resilience, continuity, or operational risk and now need to quantify decisions more rigorously.
prerequisites: Participants should have a working familiarity with emergency planning, operational risk, or business continuity concepts. Prior exposure to incident response, continuity planning, or risk registers is helpful, and no coding or programming is required for completion. If available, bring existing crisis plans, impact assessment notes, incident logs, continuity checklists, or any internal risk scoring templates so you can apply the methods directly to your environment.
